title: Taints and tolerations: reserving a node for a specific workload

videos.script: Lesson 29 was about pods choosing nodes. This one is the other direction: a node refusing pods. {{other}} A taint is a mark on a node that says keep away. A pod that does not tolerate it is not scheduled there. {{taint}} A toleration is the pod's answer: I accept that mark. It lets the pod in. It does not send it there. {{toleration}} That difference is the most common mistake with taints, and you will see why. You will reserve a node for a reports job, then mark another node for maintenance and watch every pod on it leave. {{plan}}
